name: Tracking
_note: The site's analytics and affiliate attribution, as ONE module rather than six script tags. The vendors are ordinary third-party SDKs that happen to ship as CDN JavaScript, which is exactly the case a module exists for: the browser lane loads their real scripts and calls their real APIs, and the native lanes reach the same vendors over HTTP because a phone has no DOM to load a script into. Same actions, same resolves, same events, three lanes (constitution, Article 10).

web._note: web/index.js IS the lane, discovered by file presence. `boot` is not a formality here: attribution has to be recorded on the FIRST page view, and a facet that registered on first call would have missed the referral that brought the visitor in.

context._note: Declared state, so markup binds `dsx.module.tracking.context.referral` instead of calling an action in on:appear and stashing the answer. Published on every lane.

ready._note: At least one vendor is configured and accepting calls. False means every call settles no-op rather than failing.

referral._note: The affiliate code that brought this visitor in, from `?via=`. Empty when the visit is direct.

visitorId._note: The analytics visitor id, when a vendor has assigned one. Empty before the first response.

goal._note: One conversion goal, fanned to every configured vendor. Fire-and-forget by design: a blocked tracker must never stall a tap.

tests.name: reports a goal to every configured vendor

referral._note: The affiliate code for this visitor, resolved from the URL on first sight and remembered for the cookie window.

tests.name: resolves empty for a direct visit

identify._note: Bind the visitor to a known person, for the support widget and for affiliate conversion.
